# libarchive / libarchive_roundtrip_fuzzer

libarchive's own fuzz target `libarchive_roundtrip_fuzzer` ([source](source/libarchive_roundtrip_fuzzer.cc), modified; see below), one of the targets OSS-Fuzz builds, over libarchive (libarchive/libarchive at 3670ecf7).

Despite its name and header comment ('tests write/read consistency'), it checks no round trip. It writes <= 5 regular files (fuzz pathname <= 32 chars, uid/gid, <= 256 data bytes) as pax_restricted/ustar/cpio newc/zip/gnutar into memory, then reads the archive back with all formats and drains the data, never comparing the read-back pathname, size, ids or bytes with what it wrote. If reserving or resizing its buffer or allocating its read buffer throws std::bad_alloc, it frees the open writer or reader, if any, and returns 0. Each call first ignores SIGPIPE, as bsdtar and bsdcpio do.

## How this program differs from what OSS-Fuzz runs
- Linked against libarchive at commit 3670ecf7.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the harness one to four times and prints each return value.
- The harness source is modified: source/libarchive_roundtrip_fuzzer.cc is libarchive 3670ecf7's contrib/oss-fuzz/libarchive_roundtrip_fuzzer.cc with two Theorem Labs changes. On std::bad_alloc it frees any open archive and returns 0; the original aborts. It ignores SIGPIPE, as bsdtar and bsdcpio do, so a write to a filter program that stopped reading fails with EPIPE instead of killing the run.

## What the harness checks
The harness makes no check of its own beyond not crashing. Its halts statements say only that the code it calls never crashes, hangs or trips a sanitizer. Its agreement statements say only that the code never crashes or trips a sanitizer, and allow a run that never ends.
